## Findings
- claim-1: The paper formally conjectures that both Theorem 5.4 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal. [source-6@L14-L16|claim=ordinary-document]
- claim-2: Conditional on the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation, in the boundary subcase \[ p=q-i=1,\qquad c=r-j\ge2,\qquad \min(i,j)=2, \] the degree-\(\le d+2\) quotient of \(Q=J/A_+J\), \(d=ij\), is \[ Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2} \cong \mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2. \] Moreover \(\bar y_1=-\bar x_1\) and \(\bar y_2=\bar x_2\).
- claim-3: This low-degree certificate alone does not imply \(Q\cong\mathbb Z^3\): a graded abelian group may agree through degree \(d+2\) and have an additional nonzero summand in degree \(d+3\).
## Strategy
Assume the integral box/Schur/Pieri presentation. For \(p=1,\ c\ge2,\ \min(i,j)=2\), compute only degrees \(d,d+1,d+2\) of \(Q=J/A_+J\).

Use
\[
(A_+J)_{d+1}=A_1J_d,\qquad
(A_+J)_{d+2}=A_2J_d+A_1J_{d+1},
\]
with \(A_1=\mathbb Zh_1\), \(A_2=\mathbb Zh_2+\mathbb Zh_1^2\), and
\[
h_1^2x_0=h_1x_1+h_1y_1.
\]
Thus the displayed \(h_1x_0,h_2x_0,h_1x_1,h_1y_1\) Pieri rows span the full positive-degree product lattice in these degrees. The unit complementary minor gives the stated integral truncated quotient.

## Gaps
This proves only
\[
Q_d\oplus Q_{d+1}\oplus Q_{d+2}\cong
\mathbb Z\bar x_0\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_1\oplus\mathbb Z\bar x_2.
\]
It does not exclude classes, torsion, or relations in degrees \(>d+2\). It therefore proves neither all-degree basis status, generation of \(J\), minimality, nor the parent theorem.

The opposite boundary \(c=1,\ p\ge2\) is not covered by this certificate.

## Next
1. Treat \(c=1,\ p\ge2\) as a separate boundary certificate, including its own complete row lattice and unimodular minor.
2. Separately prove an all-degree graded-kernel/saturation or elimination argument for \(Q\).
3. Apply graded Nakayama only after all-degree integral basis status and generation are independently established.
